verdicts.title: Spectral lower bounds for the orthogonal and projective ranks of a graph
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: The orthogonal rank of a graph $G=(V,E)$ is the smallest dimension $ξ$ such that there exist non-zero column vectors $x_v\in\mathbb{C}^ξ$ for $v\in V$ satisfying the orthogonality condition $x_v^\dagger x_w=0$ for all $vw\in E$. We prove that many spectral lower bounds for the chromatic number, $χ$, are also lower bounds for $ξ$. This result complements a previous result by the authors, in which they showed that spectral lower bounds for $χ$ are also lower bounds for the quantum chromatic number
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns spectral lower bounds for orthogonal/projective ranks of graphs in the context of chromatic number variants, which shares only the generic vocabulary of 'spectral' and 'rank' with the conjecture's hypercontractive stable-rank DNF invariant. It says nothing about Bonami–Beckner kernels, DNF term supports, or monotone clique formula complexity.

verdicts.title: Adaptive Lower Bound for Testing Monotonicity on the Line
verdicts.abstract_excerpt:
In the property testing model, the task is to distinguish objects possessing some property from the objects that are far from it. One of such properties is monotonicity, when the objects are functions from one poset to another. This is an active area of research. In this paper we study query complexity of $ε$-testing monotonicity of a function $f\colon [n]\to[r]$. All our lower bounds are for adaptive two-sided testers.

verdicts.title: Around Operator Monotone Functions
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We show that the symmetrized product $AB+BA$ of two positive operators $A$ and $B$ is positive if and only if $f(A+B)\leq f(A)+f(B)$ for all non-negative operator monotone functions $f$ on $[0,\infty)$ and deduce an operator inequality. We also give a necessary and sufficient condition for that the composition $f\circ g$ of an operator convex function $f$ on $[0,\infty)$ and a non-negative operator monotone function $g$ on an interval $(a,b)$ is operator monotone and give some applications.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns operator monotone/convex functions and symmetrized products of positive operators, with no reference to DNFs, Fourier/noise operators, stable rank, or clique complexity. It shares no specific claim with the conjecture about Bonami–Beckner term-correlation Gram matrices.
